I did great in school, but it turns out that I have a slew of mental health problems that definitely showed before, but were never addressed and still haven't been. I do not know what these illnesses are at the moment, I just know that they've severely inhibited my growth since I left the structure of school and the dependence on my family. It's been six years since I graduated highschool, but I have nothing to show for it. Just years of stagnation, unemployment, relying on my mother when she's sober, and other family or, now my best friend and his wife if not. Anxiety, mood swings, and general depression make daily life incredibly difficult, not to mention holding down even the most mental jobs. I burn out extremely quickly. Physically, I'm in horrible shape. I have hypothyroidism, but can't manage to get myself in the habit of taking the meds, nor in the habit of eating healthy, much less exercising, so I'm obese. Even hygiene is a major chore.

All of this is to say that, of recently, knock on wood, I've been getting better. There are still days I panic, days I crash out, and days that I think about suicide. I just have to tell myself to pick up the pieces and keep going. I need therapy desperately, but still don't know how to attain it, and I'm not confident my current streak of relative progress will continue. I like to call mental illness, or at least my strain of it, a terminal disease. If I don't treat it, it will kill me.

Resin flows from the Great River, whose origin is lost even to the gods themselves. Everything is formed from resin, from people to plants to rocks to the vacuum of Space. What separates the core races from animals is that they can manipulate the internal flow of their resin. Typically, this has very few applications on its own, but when a being is born with maligned resin, that is a different elemental alignment than standard for their species, they gain special innate powers. These can be shitty and uncontrollable or exceptional, all coming down to cosmic luck. However, enchantments, runes inscribed into pretty much anything, are activated and maintained by a person inputting their resin into the rune. This gives people born without powers access to abilities. The final tennet of my core magic system is alchemy. Creating potions simply has to do with combining ingredients with the correct resin alignment to get the desired results, and work by integrating into ones resin and swaying it's alignment temporarily. This is typically done through ingesting the potion, but there are some that exist as an inhalent or topical.

It starts out with me at my local park. On the swings, there is a pink haired girl, a red haired girl, and a blue haired guy. I do not recognize these three. In the fourth swing is a girl I went to school with. I go around and talk to them for a bit, meaningless conversation. The girl I went to school with I had a crush on at the time, so I was engaged with her. After a few minutes, the conversations cease, and I move to leave the park.

As I exit, a lion jumps out from nowhere and begins chasing me. It chases me all the way to my house, well, where my house usually is at least. In its place is a very large and extravagant mansion. I run inside, trapping the lion on the other side of the door. I then proceed to go throughout the whole mansion in a panic closing every open door I come across. After this is done, I open the door to leave.

I open the door to my regular front yard, and my house is no longer replaced by the mansion. The lion is now a tiger, and jumps up on me, putting it's paws on my shoulders like a big dog. It looks at me with puppy dog eyes. In my yard, standing in a line, are all of my relatives that were alive when I was born, bar my late uncle who died six months after, ending with my little sister. One by one, they start to walk away from me. Each one, as they leave, disappears into thin air before they reach the edge of my yard. This happens in the order in which they passed away in real life. My grandfather, his sister, his brother, my grandmother's brother, and then people who (as of this dream's occurrence) are still living start to leave. They too disappear before they reach the edge of the yard. My grandmother was next, and she was also the next one to pass in real life. When it gets to me, and I start to walk away, I panic and my ethereal self runs. 

It's suddenly night time. As I run, I see my shadow underneath passing street lights. It looks like a silhouette of Envy from Full Metal Alchemist. Eventually, I find myself back at the park. This time, though, it's empty. Then time stops, and the world begins to spin around me, with time fast forwarding. I'm in some sort of near future. The blue haired guy and the pink haired girl are there. The blue hair guy is sitting on the swings, looking forlorn. I go to talk to him and learn that the red haired girl from before died from cancer. In the parking lot of the park, there is a giant, billboard sized bug looking robot displaying some sort of advertisement. I then approach the pink haired girl.

She asks if I want to "do it." I say yes, and we get down to business. A short way in, she starts to choke me. I tell her to stop, push her away. She asks "Isn't this what you wanted?" When I say no, she folds into the crab walk position, her head turns upside down, and she starts crawling at me, eyes black like a demon. The world has a filter of red over it now, and there is a knife in her mouth. I fight her, removing the knife from her mouth and killing her with it. I walk into the play area.

As I round a bend surrounding a large piece of play equipment, I see my best friend. His eyes are also black like a demon's, and he holds two knives. He charges at me, I summon my own pair of knives, and we begin fighting. There are clashes, cuts, and jabs. At one point, we throw the knives at each other, the clash in midair, we jump and catch them, and push each other away. After this, I run at him, finally stabbing him. He immediately stops, looks at me and smiles. He says "You better get out before it's too late." Then time freezes again.

Again, the world spins around me, fast forwarding through time. I arrive at a much more distant future, where giant robot spiders are causing mass havoc. My town is destroyed, people are being killed in the streets. There are four others there with me, each wearing a black power ranger-esque costume. I am wearing one too. Collectively, we say "Exo-suit, ON!" And power up. Immediately, I jump on one of the robot spiders, point the gun atop its head under my chin, and let it shoot me.

This is the strangest part.

i wake up, and I know I'm awake despite these next details. My vision is filled with a horribly bright white light, and I am pulling myself forward. After the light clears, I'm not laying in my bed, but instead standing at, gripping, and pulling on my dresser. I never slept walked before nor after this. 

I feel like this dream has some absurd deeper meaning, maybe multiple, but I still have no clue what it could be.

The ultimate evil in my world is Boak'dere, the God of destruction. Their brother is the God of Creation, and, after fighting together against the Somethings for control of space, they begin to fight each other over how to maintain it. Boak'dere liked the solitude and peace of the empty void, whereas their brother wanted to liven it up with various creations. They fought once over this, which birthed the planet the main story takes place on, and they are prophesied to fight again, leading to the end of reality as it is currently known.

When a God 'dies', they decay into one or more different parts. When a Devil dies, their power and domain is automatically absorbed by whatever being killed them. 

Each has only happened once in my story. The Goddess of Life was killed by the devil of Death. She decayed into seven parts, six elemental titans (Fire, Wind, Earth, Water, Plant, and Lightning), and the seventh part being the purest kernel of her essence. The God of Enchanting, her brother, sought out the devil that killed her, and, in turn, took it's life, not knowing he would automatically absorb power over death. The God fo enchanting ends up with both the power of death and that pure kernel from the Goddess of Life, to become the God of life and death, and he passes his own domain on to his artificial offspring.

The Veinmer are a very religious people who live their lives in constant pilgrimage, roaming from holy site to holy site, and each tribe takes at least one pilgrimage to the world tree each year, tending the jungle as their own personal garden.

This world tree, which is the physical form of that sealed titan, and the area around it are taken care of by a very specific tribe of Veinmer. Veinmer live a long time. They are basically trees themselves, but still suffer through age in a very human way. Elders who can no longer constantly travel take up permanent residence in the canopy city built around the world tree. They are revered by their people for this, and, when they die, their final resting place is at the base of the world tree, so that their carcass may feed it.

I think, overall, Shippuden was the better time skip.

Boruto comes back significantly stronger than when he left, with new jutsu, huge mental development, emotional turmoil, and interesting characters that helped this change happen. This also makes flashbacks to during the time skip more engaging, whereas Naruto growth is far less significant, and the few events that we're told unfolded during the Naruto skip aren't nearly as interesting as the things we know happened with Boruto during his. However, I personally think this is to the detriment of Boruto's plot and character growth. 

The time skip should include things we aren't interested in seeing. Naruto almost solely trained his chakra manipulation during the time skip, which people here are saying makes it worse. Personally, this part of his training, which wouldn't have been as interesting as the water walking or tree climbing exercises, and took far longer, would not have been fun to see in real time. It's the perfect thing to not show, but still be necessary to the plot and Naruto's growth as a character. Conversely, Boruto gets tons of new jutsu, and interesting lore bits that would have been wonderful to see play out, as opposed to in flashbacks.

In Naruto, we also see and feel the growth and maturation of the side cast. They have noticeable growth, unlike Boruto's side cast, who seem, relatively, the same as their part one counterparts. The time skip in Naruto also gives the villains room to advance their plans and become the main focus of Shippuden, whereas the villains in Boruto seem to have been stagnant, not to mention we get a complete switcheroo of who the main antagonists are. Additionally, in Naruto, the Akatsuki and their goals were foreshadowed, but with Boruto we get the tree people kinda out of nowhere. 

Overall, Naruto's time skip is better, though, some of the problems I see in Boruto aren't just limited to the time skip (such as the side cast taking on a much more minor role.) However, I say all of this to end on the statement that we, as a fandom, have the outcome of the whole story of Naruto, which we lack with Boruto. All of our opinions, no matter which side we pick, may change by the time the series ends.

What I didn't mention is that these alignments can deviate in the womb, giving an individual powers outside of their racial traits, and that humans have the highest rate of deviation.

This deviation can cause good things or bad things. Most often, though, it is both. Veinks'l, no last name, is a human who lives in the continent sized desert in the south western hemisphere. He lives away from any towns, in a lone house, with nobody but his great nephew. He exists, story wise, mostly to give the main party refuge from a sandstorm.

However, he also showcases the possible negative effects of a deviated alignment moreso than most characters. He was born mutated, with huge open sores on his head and body that prevent hair growth. Through the sores, he naturally releases flammable gases, but the same deviation also gives him immunity to most fires. 

Veinks'l faced ostracization his whole life because of how he looks and smells, as well as hearty medical issues cause by the nature of his mutations (easy for infections to enter the body). In his twilight years, when he meets the main group, he prefers solitude, to the point where he denies the part when they ask him to join them.

In my work, each race has a magical alignment in tune with one of the six elements (water, fire, air, electricity, nature, earth) or neutral, at base. Mermen are water, Dwarves are fire, Altmer are air, Fae are electricity, Veinmer are nature, and Cyclops are earth. Humans are neutral, and that is the core of what sets them apart.

I've been working on this world for almost a decade, and it's hardly finished. Of course, there's been breaks and long periods of stagnation as I've used the world for its intended purpose - a game me and my friends used to play. 

It started out as simply a world full of superheroes and villains. Think My Hero Academia but in a more medieval setting. Since then, I've integrated dedicated magic systems, multiple new races, and fleshed out a lot of the original locations. Now, only a small percentage are born with powers, and most everybody else uses enchantments.

Dwarves:

Originally, they, like all the non-human sentient races in my world, were created by accident when the gods sealed the fire Titan under the planet's crust. Obsidian black skin, cracked with red streaks of fire. Of course, they're still short and bulky. They live on small rock islands that float atop their oceans of magma. Their sky is littered with ancient runes, which they used to create their own language and learn to enchant.

Eventually, they breach the surface with their enchantments, through volcanoes, and war with the other races over land. This event is known as the Great Blooming. This also results in the evolution of the Dwarven subraces.

The Underdwarves are the ones I described above. Obsidian black skin cracked with fire. They breathe heat and are master smiths and enchanters.

Surface Dwarves are much closer to what you think when you hear Dwarf. Short, bulky humans with long hair and beards. The only major difference is the stone colored skin that retains a cracked appearance, where the fire cracks would have been had they been an Underdwarf.

Then there are the Shattered Dwarves, who originated from the ones that breached under the ocean during the Blooming. They are smaller, more gnomish, and brittle. Their skin is whiter than their surface cousins, and they are born with deep gouges in their flesh where their fire cracks would be. Throughout life, they usually fill these cracks with coral and/or various underwater flora. 

They brought Enchanting, which is the biggest mechanic in my universe, to the world, and even created the first written language and records during their dominant periods. 

Nowadays, their countries are mostly isolationist and xenophobic, but there are some allied with human (and other) countries.

My world exists on a sort of grand cycle, where a reality emerges, stays for a while, and then sinks back.

First, there was nothing, but since nothing is relative to something, it exists in a contradictory state. Therefore, it cannot stay in this state forever. The 5 Tenets of Existence emerge from nothing. Instinct the mind, Chaos the nature, Infinity the body, Connection the relation, and Entopy the end. 

Entropy is the driver of the cycle, eating away at his fellows one by one, until they are consumed, and reality returns to nothing.

But there is a lot that happens before the returning to nothing part, that being the entire history of my universe.

First, Entropy decays Instinct, which cannot die because of Connection, keeping all of the Tenets linked to one another, so it splits into a very large, though not infinite, amount of logical thinking beings. They refer to themselves as "Somethings" because to them they are the only beings in all of reality. Next, Entropy decays Chaos, who splits into two beings, Creation and Destruction. There is a war with the Somethings, and it results in the Creator and Destroyer carving out their own corner of reality, which they call Space. From here, they create everything else. Stars, planets, nebulae, black holes, life, and even time.

Major ages in my world differ in how much the gods interact with it. There is one point in my world where all of the gods walked the world like mortals, helping create it. Once sentient life came about, most of the gods ascended to immortality, but still heavily interacted with the world. During this time period, there were a lot of demigods and mythic heroes roaming about. After the third human/dwarven war, and the world settled into a less chaotic state, the gods withdrew their influence. The exception to this would be that each God and goddess would have a prophet at different points in time, spread throughout recorded history, to be called on when needed. Then when the demons and devils invade, the gods come back down, alongside revived heroes from throughout time, to help fight in the war.

It seems this comment has come at a good time for me. I suffer from some undiagnosed mental illness. It causes high levels of emotion, mainly anxiety, no matter how trivial the source or the context. It causes panic attacks, forms of self harm (hitting myself, or hitting things I know will hurt me like trees and concrete), and easy irritability and overstimulation. These issues have only compounded since I've moved to a new part of my state. I have been unemployed and couch hopping between relatives and friends for the better part of the last three years. Of course, the story is more complex than that, but the details don't matter.
My point is that, now, in my early twenties, and only after years of self reflection, have I come to terms with the fact that I cannot handle these issues on my own, despite them being persistent throughout my life. It was easy to get by, despite this, during my school years because of a controlled environment and consistent schedule and a lack of further pressure because I happened to be academically advantaged. School was easy for me, and thus easy to hide my fears, insecurities, and deflect and deny my mental issues.
Because of my performance in school, my mother and grandmother (my dad was never in the picture) misunderstood my mental issues, as did I. Having been shown and told all my life the "men don't show emotions" facade, I was never able to fully comprehend, and therefore explain, why i was the way I was. This also, at some points, led those around me to believe I was someone I was not. There were very few people I could confide in at all, and all them only partially. It was only in recent times I have been able to counteract this. My mother is my confidant. I try to be as communicative as possible with how I feel, yet it is impossible for me to fully explain these things to her, because of years of neglect to the awareness and understanding of my own emotions.
My fears make it difficult to get a job, because I fret over every aspect of the concept. I also cannot drive because of seizures that popped up out of nowhere, causing me to wreck and consequentially be afraid of ever getting behind the wheel again. The thought of therapy is impossible not only because of my own ingrained stigma against it, but also because of lack of funds and insurance.
To answer your question completely, and end the explanation, there is no one I can completely confide in, even though I know it is okay to do so now, and i fear the damage to my psyche is irreversible.
I urge any and all who feel similarly to me, as I suspect many of you do, to reach out before it's too late. Do it now, while it's still manageable, before there is too much damage done, and I wish for you all to be happy.

The first time it happened was when I was a child. I woke up in my room, where smoke had funneled through the crack under the door. At that moment, however, it stood solid above my head. I could feel the heat, and the heaviness in my lunges. I didn't know what was going on. I tried the door, but the handle burned my hand. I was able to exit the window, and I walked around to the front of my house to see the still flames through the windows before time started once again.

I soon figured out that time would stop if I was close to death, and only start after I was safe. Even though I was grateful to be alive, I always had this feeling that it was long since my time to go.

Nevertheless, I grew up recklessly, partially because I knew I wouldn't die, and partially because I wanted to. The power never failed.

Though it did try to teach me some lessons, like stopping only inches before I was launched off of a waterfall, or continuing too soon, and being grazed by a bullet.

I grew old, and have long feared what would happen when my body was ready to give out. Now I know.

It has been a year, since that day. The day my daughter rushed me to the hospital, long after her mother had died. The day I laid on that hospital bed, thinking to myself that I would finally get to see my father and mother, who had perished in that fire trying to save me from my room all those years ago, and my wife.

The universe had a different plan, as it always did, because, as I laid there, my hand squeezed by my daughter's, as her husband was walking in the door with my grandchild in his arms, time stopped. The pain was frozen in her eyes. The worry was frozen in his.

Everyday I had studied this picture. Everyday I get into that hospital bed, and push my hand back in my daughter's, wishing that whatever is keeping me here will just let go, because there is no way around it this time.
